lp_hero_title: Join the Movement Empowering Digital Careers.
lp_review_1: Shaktipath helped me start my WhatsApp boutique in just 3 days. The lessons are so easy to follow!
lp_review_2: I got my first freelance data entry gig thanks to the Gig Finder tool. Highly recommended.
sm_l1_intro: The navigation bar is the steering wheel of your phone. It consists of three shapes at the bottom of your screen. 1. The Triangle (Back) acts like an 'Undo' button, taking you to the previous screen. 2. The Circle (Home) is your escape hatch; no matter where you are, it instantly takes you back to your main dashboard. 3. The Square (Recent Apps) shows you all the apps currently running, allowing you to switch between tasks like flipping through pages of a book. Mastering these three buttons is the first step to digital fluency.
sm_l1_goal_list: Identify the 3 main buttons | Understand their functions
sm_l1_action_list: Tap the Triangle (Back) to go back | Tap the Circle (Home) to exit | Tap the Square (Recent) to see open apps
sm_l1_task_desc: Find the Home button on your phone. Press it. Then press the Recent button and close one app.
sm_l1_quiz_q: Which button takes you to the main screen?
sm_l2_intro: Your phone contains a control center called the 'Quick Settings' panel, usually hidden at the top of the screen. This panel gives you instant access to essential utilities like WiFi, Bluetooth, and Sound. A critical control here is 'Brightness'. High brightness consumes battery rapidly and can strain your eyes in dark environments. Conversely, low brightness saves battery but makes the screen illegible outdoors. Learning to adjust this dynamically is key to comfortable usage.
sm_l2_goal_list: How to open settings | How to change brightness
sm_l2_action_list: Swipe down from top | Slide the sun icon to change brightness | Turn on 'Eye Comfort' mode at night
sm_l2_task_desc: Set your brightness to 50%. Find and turn on 'Silent Mode' for 1 minute.
sm_l2_quiz_q: How do you open quick settings?
sm_l3_intro: The internet reaches your phone via two distinct pipes. 'Mobile Data' is provided by your SIM carrier (like Jio or Airtel) and connects you to cell towers; it works anywhere but costs money per Gigabyte. 'WiFi' connects your phone to a local broadband router; it offers high speed, lower cost, and stability, but only works within a short range (like inside a home or office). Switching to WiFi for heavy tasks like downloading videos is a smart financial habit.
sm_l3_goal_list: Difference between WiFi and Data | How to connect
sm_l3_action_list: Tap Settings > WiFi | Turn it ON | Select a network and enter password
sm_l3_task_desc: Turn off your Mobile Data and try to connect to a WiFi network.
sm_l3_quiz_q: What is faster and cheaper for downloads?
sm_l4_intro: Think of the Google Play Store as a secure digital supermarket. Unlike downloading files from random websites which might carry viruses (malware), apps on the Play Store are scanned for safety. When choosing an app, always verify its credibility by checking the 'Star Rating' (4+ is good) and the 'Number of Downloads'. A high download count indicates that millions of users trust the app.
sm_l4_goal_list: How to search for apps | How to install safely
sm_l4_action_list: Open Play Store | Search for 'Calculator' | Tap Install | Wait for 'Open' button
sm_l4_task_desc: Search for 'Google Translate' in the Play Store. Read one review.
sm_l4_quiz_q: Where do you get safe apps?
sm_l5_intro: For professionals, WhatsApp is a filing cabinet, not just a chat room. As you receive hundreds of messages, important information gets buried. 'Pinning' a chat keeps your most important contact (like your boss) permanently at the top. 'Starring' a message acts like a bookmark, saving a specific address or instruction into a separate 'Starred Messages' list so you don't have to scroll endlessly to find it later.
sm_l5_action_list: Pin a chat to top | Star a message to save it | Send a location
sm_l5_task_desc: Find an important message. Star it. Then go to Settings > Starred Messages to find it.
sm_l5_quiz_q: How to save a specific message?
sm_l6_intro: YouTube is the world's largest free library of video tutorials. You can find visual instructions for almost any skill. However, video streaming consumes significant data. By manually adjusting the 'Video Quality' setting (e.g., lowering it from 1080p High Definition to 360p Standard Definition), you can reduce data consumption by up to 80% while still understanding the audio content perfectly.
sm_l6_action_list: Tap Search icon | Type 'How to cook rice' | Use the mic to speak your search
sm_l6_task_desc: Search for 'Excel basics'. Change the video quality to 360p to save data.
sm_l6_quiz_q: Can you learn skills on YouTube?
sm_l7_intro: Photography is painting with light. The most common mistake is having the light source behind the subject, creating a silhouette. Always keep the light source behind YOU, the photographer. Additionally, smartphone cameras need guidance; tapping the screen on the most important part of the image (like a face or text) tells the computer where to lock 'Focus' and 'Exposure', ensuring clarity.
sm_l7_action_list: Clean the lens with a cloth | Tap screen to focus | Hold steady and snap
sm_l7_task_desc: Take a photo of a notebook text. Make sure it is readable.
sm_l8_intro: Voice Search utilizes Natural Language Processing (NLP) to understand spoken human language. Instead of typing keywords, you can speak full sentences to Google Assistant. This is particularly powerful for users who find typing in English difficult or slow. It can perform actions like 'Call Mom' or answer queries like 'What is the weather?', acting as a hands-free personal butler.
sm_l8_action_list: Tap the Mic icon on Google bar | Say 'What is the weather?' | Say 'Call Mom'
sm_l8_task_desc: Ask Google: 'How far is Delhi from Mumbai?' using your voice.
sm_l9_intro: Digital security operates on authentication: proving you are who you say you are. A Screen Lock (PIN, Pattern, or Biometric) is the first line of defense. Without it, if your phone is lost, a stranger has instant access to your emails, photos, and banking apps. Using simple PINs like '1234' or '0000' is like leaving your house key under the doormat—easily guessed by thieves.
sm_l9_goal_list: Setting a screen lock | PIN safety
sm_l9_action_list: Go to Settings > Security | Set a Screen Lock (PIN/Pattern) | Don't use '1234'
sm_l9_task_desc: Ensure your phone locks automatically after 1 minute of no use.
comp_l1_intro: Computers come in two form factors. A 'Desktop' is a modular system where the screen (Monitor), input devices (Keyboard/Mouse), and brain (CPU Tower) are separate. It requires constant power. A 'Laptop' is an all-in-one portable unit with a built-in battery. While laptops offer mobility, desktops often offer more power for the same price and are easier to repair.
comp_l1_goal_list: Types of computers | Parts of a computer
comp_l1_action_list: Identify screen (Monitor) | Identify typing board (Keyboard) | Identify pointer tool (Mouse)
comp_l1_task_desc: Look at a computer. Find the power button.
comp_l2_intro: A computer is not like a light bulb; it has a complex operating system that needs to 'Boot Up' (load) and 'Shut Down' (save and close). Cutting power directly can corrupt files or damage the hard drive. The 'Shut Down' command sends a signal to all running programs to close their tasks safely before the machine powers off.
comp_l2_action_list: Press Power Button | Wait for screen | Click Start > Power > Shut Down
comp_l2_task_desc: Turn on a computer, wait for it to load, then turn it off properly.
comp_l3_intro: The mouse acts as your digital hand. It has two primary buttons. The 'Left Click' is your action finger—used to select, drag, or open items. The 'Right Click' is your information finger—it opens a 'Context Menu' specific to whatever you clicked on, offering options like Copy, Paste, or Properties. The Scroll Wheel helps you navigate long pages without moving the cursor.
comp_l3_action_list: Left click to select | Double left click to open | Right click for menu
comp_l3_task_desc: Right click on the desktop and select 'Refresh'.
comp_l4_intro: The keyboard is divided into zones: Alphanumeric (letters/numbers), Navigation (arrows), and Function keys. Special command keys are crucial: 'Enter' executes a command or creates a new line. 'Backspace' deletes text to the left. 'Spacebar' creates separation. 'Shift' modifies keys (e.g., making letters capital or typing the symbol above a number).
comp_l4_action_list: Find 'Enter' (Go to next line) | Find 'Backspace' (Erase) | Find 'Spacebar' (Add space)
comp_l4_task_desc: Open Notepad and type your full name.
comp_l5_intro: The 'Desktop' is the main workspace of your Operating System (OS). Think of it like a physical desk. 'Icons' are visual shortcuts representing files, folders, or programs. You can arrange them, stack them, or throw them in the 'Recycle Bin' (trash). Keeping a clean desktop helps you find important work quickly.
comp_l5_action_list: Identify 'This PC' | Identify 'Recycle Bin' | Drag an icon to move it
comp_l5_task_desc: Move the Recycle Bin icon to a different corner of the screen.
comp_l6_intro: The 'Start Menu' is the central hub of Windows. It lists every installed application alphabetically. The 'Search Bar' next to it is the fastest way to find tools; instead of hunting through lists, you simply type the name of the app (e.g., 'Word') and press Enter. This 'Search-first' workflow is a hallmark of advanced users.
comp_l6_action_list: Click Start button (Windows logo) | Type 'Paint' | Click to open
comp_l6_task_desc: Open the 'Calculator' app on your computer.
comp_l7_intro: The Graphical User Interface (GUI) uses 'Windows'—rectangular boxes that hold programs. You manage these with three universal controls: Minimize (_) hides the window to the taskbar without closing it. Maximize (□) expands it to fill the entire screen for focus. Close (X) terminates the program completely. Mastering these controls allows you to multitask effectively.
comp_l7_action_list: Click '-' to hide window | Click square to full screen | Click 'X' to close
comp_l7_task_desc: Open a window, make it full screen, then close it.
comp_l8_intro: Efficient typing requires understanding case control. The 'Shift' key is a temporary modifier—you hold it down to type a single capital letter or a symbol (like @ or %). 'Caps Lock' is a toggle switch—you press it once to type EVERYTHING in capitals, and press it again to stop. Confusing these two often leads to password errors.
comp_l8_action_list: Press Caps Lock for BIG LETTERS | Hold Shift for one Big Letter | Hold Shift for top symbols (@, #)
comp_l8_task_desc: Type: 'Hello World!' (Pay attention to capital letters and symbol).
comp_l9_intro: Computer memory (RAM) is temporary; it is wiped when power is lost. Storage (Hard Drive) is permanent. 'Saving' writes data from RAM to Storage. 'Save As' allows you to define the name and location of a new file. 'Save' (Ctrl+S) quickly updates an existing file. Frequent saving prevents data loss during power cuts.
comp_l9_goal_list: Save vs Save As | Naming files
comp_l9_action_list: Click File > Save | Choose location (Desktop) | Give a name | Click Save
comp_l9_task_desc: Write a note in Notepad and save it as 'MyNote' on Desktop.
eng_l1_intro: Greetings set the tone for communication. In a professional setting, time-based greetings ('Good Morning', 'Good Afternoon') show respect and awareness. 'Hello' is neutral and acceptable, while 'Hi' is casual. The closing 'Goodbye' or 'Have a nice day' ensures a polite end to the interaction, leaving a positive lasting impression.
eng_l1_action_list: Say 'Hello' to friends | Say 'Good Morning' to boss | Say 'Goodbye' when leaving
eng_l2_intro: A professional introduction is your elevator pitch. It follows a simple structure: Identity (Name), Origin (City/Country), and Profession (Job/Role). Clarity is key. Instead of a long story, a concise 'I am [Name], a [Role] from [Place]' gives people the exact context they need to interact with you.
eng_l2_goal_list: My name is... | I am from...
eng_l2_action_list: Say 'My name is [Name]' | Say 'I live in [City]' | Smile while speaking
eng_l2_task_desc: Introduce yourself to a mirror clearly.
eng_l3_intro: In English business culture, direct commands can sound rude. Softeners are essential. 'Give me the file' sounds aggressive; 'Please give me the file' sounds professional. 'Thank you' acknowledges effort. 'Sorry' takes accountability. These three words act as social lubricant, reducing friction in workplace relationships.
eng_l3_action_list: Use 'Please' when asking | Use 'Thank you' when receiving | Use 'Sorry' for mistakes
eng_l3_task_desc: Ask for a glass of water using 'Please'.
eng_l4_intro: Demonstrative pronouns help us identify objects in space. 'This' refers to a singular object near you (within reach). 'That' refers to a singular object far from you (out of reach). Mastering this distinction helps in giving clear instructions, like 'Sign *this* paper here' vs 'Bring *that* box from over there'.
eng_l4_action_list: Point near: 'This is a pen' | Point far: 'That is a door' | Ask: 'What is this?'
eng_l4_task_desc: Name 5 objects in your room in English.
eng_l5_intro: Accuracy with numbers is vital for prices, dates, and times. English numbers 13-19 end in 'teen' (stress on the end), while multiples of ten (30, 40, 50) end in 'ty' (stress on the start). Confusing 'Fifteen' (15) with 'Fifty' (50) is a common and costly mistake in business. Clear pronunciation ensures financial accuracy.
eng_l5_action_list: Count fingers: One, Two, Three... | Read a price tag: 'Fifty Rupees'
eng_l5_task_desc: Read your phone number aloud in English.
eng_l6_intro: Time management relies on specific vocabulary. Prepositions are key: we use 'ON' for days (On Monday) and 'AT' for times (At 5 PM). Understanding terms like 'Quarter past' (15 mins after) or 'Half past' (30 mins after) helps in scheduling. A mix-up here leads to missed interviews or meetings.
eng_l6_action_list: Say today's day | Say 'It is 5 O'clock' | Morning/Afternoon/Evening
eng_l6_task_desc: Tell someone the current time in English.
eng_l7_intro: Every industry has jargon. Basic office vocabulary allows you to navigate the workspace. A 'Colleague' is a peer. A 'Supervisor' is a boss. A 'Client' is a customer. 'Salary' is monthly pay, while 'Wage' is hourly pay. Using the correct term shows professionalism and that you belong in the environment.
eng_l7_action_list: Office = Place of work | Colleague = Coworker | Salary = Pay
eng_l7_task_desc: Describe your dream job in 1 sentence.
eng_l8_intro: Business chats (SMS/WhatsApp) often use acronyms for speed. 'ASAP' (As Soon As Possible) conveys urgency. 'FYI' (For Your Information) implies no action is needed. 'EOD' (End Of Day) sets a deadline. Decoding these quickly is essential to prioritizing your tasks effectively.
eng_l8_action_list: Read 'Call me later' | Read 'Meeting at 5 PM' | Understand urgency
eng_l8_task_desc: Read the last English SMS you received.
eng_l9_intro: In business, brevity is a virtue. You do not need flowery language. A confirmation ('Received, thanks'), a negation ('No, I cannot do that'), or an agreement ('Yes, that works') is sufficient. The goal of a reply is to close the loop of communication clearly and quickly.
eng_l9_action_list: Reply 'Yes, I can' | Reply 'No, sorry' | Reply 'Ok, noted'
eng_l9_task_desc: Reply to a friend's message in English.
free_l1_intro: Freelancing is a shift from 'selling your time' to 'selling a service'. Unlike an employee who gets paid to show up, a freelancer gets paid to deliver a result (a logo, a translation, a spreadsheet). It offers location freedom but requires self-discipline, as you are responsible for finding work and managing your own schedule.
free_l1_action_list: Imagine working from home | You are your own boss | You must find clients
free_l1_task_desc: Tell a friend: 'Freelancing means working for myself using the internet.'
free_l1_quiz_q: In freelancing, who is the boss?
free_l2_intro: The digital economy values 'Hard Skills'. A hard skill is something teachable and measurable, like typing speed, proficiency in Photoshop, or ability to translate Hindi to English. Start by auditing yourself: What can you do on a computer that others might pay for? Even basic skills like organizing email have market value.
free_l2_action_list: Can you type? | Can you design? | Can you speak English? These are skills.
free_l2_task_desc: Write down 3 things you are good at.
free_l3_intro: Your infrastructure determines your capabilities. A smartphone allows for communication, social media management, and simple writing. A laptop unlocks higher-paying gigs like complex data entry, graphic design, and programming. A stable internet connection is your lifeline; without it, you are disconnected from the marketplace.
free_l3_action_list: Check if phone works well | Check internet speed | Install Zoom/Google Meet
free_l3_task_desc: Ensure you have a quiet corner to work.
free_l4_intro: The internet has predators. A universal rule of employment is: Money flows from Employer to Employee. If a 'client' asks you to pay a registration fee, security deposit, or for an 'ID card' before working, it is a scam. legitimate clients will interview you and pay you for your work, never the other way around.
free_l4_goal_list: Identifying fakes | Never paying to work
free_l4_action_list: Real jobs pay YOU | Scams ask YOU to pay | Don't share OTPs
free_l4_task_desc: Remember: If someone asks for money to give a job, say NO.
free_l5_intro: The gig economy is vast. 'Data Entry' is digitizing information. 'Transcription' is converting audio to text. 'Virtual Assistance' is remote administrative support. 'Content Moderation' is keeping forums safe. 'Translation' is bridging languages. Choose a niche that aligns with your existing abilities to start earning quickly.
free_l5_action_list: Data Entry: Typing numbers | VA: Managing emails | Translation: Changing languages
free_l5_task_desc: Pick one job type you like.
free_l6_intro: In traditional jobs, you learn once and work for years. In freelancing, technology changes monthly. To stay relevant and increase your rates, you must be an infinite learner. Using free resources like YouTube to learn a new software feature (upskilling) directly correlates to your ability to charge higher prices.
free_l6_action_list: Search 'How to use Excel' | Practice daily | Better skills = More money
free_l6_task_desc: Watch one 5-minute tutorial on a new skill today.
free_l7_intro: In a remote environment, you are judged solely by your output and communication. Professionalism means 'Reliability'. If you promise a file by 5 PM, delivering it by 5 PM builds trust. Delivering it at 6 PM destroys it. Polite, timely, and reliable communication is your personal brand.
free_l7_action_list: Be polite | Submit work on time | Reply fast
free_l7_task_desc: Send a professional message to a friend practicing.
free_l8_intro: You are running a business of one. You must have the infrastructure to receive funds. In India, a Bank Account linked to UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is standard. For international clients, a gateway like PayPal is often required. Always clarify payment terms (Rate, Method, Date) *before* starting any work.
free_l8_action_list: Have a bank account | Share UPI ID only | Keep records
free_l8_task_desc: Check if your UPI is active.
free_l9_intro: Analysis paralysis is the enemy. The best way to start is to start. Create a simple profile (Bio + Photo) describing your service. Announce your availability to your immediate network (friends, family, old colleagues). Your first client is statistically likely to be someone you already know.
free_l9_action_list: Write a short bio | Take a clear photo | Look for gigs
free_l9_task_desc: Write 2 lines about yourself for a job profile.
mon_l1_intro: Financial literacy starts with recognizing value. Indian currency has distinct features to prevent counterfeiting. Security threads, watermarks, and latent images on high-value notes (₹500, ₹2000) are designed for verification. Habitually checking these features prevents financial loss from fake currency.
mon_l1_action_list: Look at a 500 note | Check the security thread | Check the watermark
mon_l1_task_desc: Identify all coins in your wallet.
mon_l2_intro: Transactional math is a daily necessity. Addition helps you verify bills. Subtraction ensures you receive the correct change. Mental math speed protects you from being short-changed by vendors. Always count cash immediately upon receipt, while still at the counter.
mon_l2_action_list: Add 10 + 20 | Calculate change from 100 for a 40 rupee item
mon_l3_intro: Budgeting is the art of prioritizing. A 'Need' is essential for survival and functioning (Rent, Food, Medicine). A 'Want' is a desire that improves quality of life but isn't urgent (New Phone, Cinema). Financial health comes from spending on Needs first and saving for Wants later.
mon_l3_action_list: Need: Food, Rent | Want: Cinema, New toy | Prioritize Needs
mon_l3_task_desc: List 3 things you bought this week. Mark them Need or Want.
mon_l4_intro: Saving is buying security for your future self. It is not about the amount, but the habit. Even small, consistent savings compound over time to create an 'Emergency Fund'. This fund prevents you from falling into debt traps (high-interest loans) when unexpected expenses like illness or repairs occur.
mon_l4_action_list: Keep a small box/jar | Put spare change daily | Don't touch it
mon_l4_task_desc: Put 10 rupees in a safe place today.
mon_l5_intro: A bank is a secure warehouse for money. Unlike a piggy bank, a Bank pays you 'Interest'—a small fee for the privilege of holding your money. It also offers a digital record (Passbook/Statement) of every rupee in and out, providing legal proof of your financial standing.
mon_l5_action_list: Bank keeps money safe | Bank gives interest (extra money) | Passbook tracks money
mon_l5_task_desc: Visit a bank nearby or look at a passbook.
mon_l6_intro: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is India's digital payment revolution. It links your phone number directly to your bank account. It allows you to send money to anyone instantly, 24/7, without knowing their bank details—just their phone number or QR code. It turns your mobile into a wallet.
mon_l6_action_list: Open UPI app | Link phone number | Set PIN
mon_l6_task_desc: Check if your phone number is linked to your bank.
mon_l7_intro: The Quick Response (QR) code is a square barcode that holds payment information. When paying merchants, scanning ensures you send money to the correct account without typing errors. Always verify the 'Merchant Name' displayed on your screen matches the shop name before entering your PIN.
mon_l7_action_list: Open Scanner in app | Point at shop QR | Check name on screen | Enter amount
mon_l7_task_desc: Scan a QR code at a shop (don't pay, just check name).
mon_l8_intro: Your UPI PIN is the digital equivalent of your signature. It authorizes money to leave your account. NEVER share it. Scammers often ask you to 'Enter PIN to Receive Money'—this is a lie. You ONLY enter a PIN to SEND money. Keeping this rule saves you from fraud.
mon_l8_action_list: Cover screen when typing | Don't tell friends | Don't write on card
mon_l8_task_desc: Memorize your PIN, do not write it down.
mon_l9_intro: You cannot manage what you do not measure. Tracking expenses means writing down every rupee spent. This reveals spending patterns (e.g., realizing you spend ₹500/month on tea). Awareness is the first step to cutting unnecessary costs and increasing savings.
mon_l9_action_list: Get a notebook | Date | Item | Amount | Total at night
mon_l9_task_desc: Write down everything you spent money on today.
data_l1_intro: A spreadsheet is a digital grid used to organize, calculate, and analyze data. Imagine a notebook that can do math automatically. It is the standard tool for business data—from inventory lists to financial budgets. Understanding spreadsheets is the most requested skill for entry-level office jobs.
data_l1_goal_list: Concept of grids | Uses of sheets
data_l1_action_list: Grid of boxes | Used for lists | Used for calculations
data_l1_task_desc: Imagine you are a shopkeeper. Write down 3 things you would list in a sheet (e.g., Item, Price).
data_l2_intro: Google Sheets is a cloud-based spreadsheet tool. 'Cloud-based' means your files live on the internet, not just your device. This allows you to access your work from any phone or computer and ensures you never lose data if your device breaks. It auto-saves every change instantly.
data_l2_goal_list: Creating a new sheet | Naming it
data_l2_action_list: Download 'Google Sheets' app | Open App | Tap '+' to create new
data_l2_task_desc: Create a new sheet and name it 'My Practice Sheet'.
data_l3_intro: Spreadsheets use a coordinate system. Vertical lines are 'Columns' (labeled A, B, C). Horizontal lines are 'Rows' (labeled 1, 2, 3). The intersection is a 'Cell' (e.g., A1, C5). Every piece of data lives in a specific cell address. This structure allows the computer to find and process information precisely.
data_l3_action_list: Find Column A (Vertical) | Find Row 1 (Horizontal) | Find Cell A1
data_l3_task_desc: Tap on cell B3. Type your name in it.
data_l4_intro: Data entry requires precision. You select a cell and type. Input can be 'Text' (Words), 'Numeric' (Values for math), or 'Formula' (Instructions). Moving between cells efficiently using 'Enter' (Down) or 'Tab' (Right) increases your entry speed significantly.
data_l4_action_list: Tap a cell | Type text or number | Press Enter/Tick
data_l4_task_desc: Type 'Apple' in A1 and '50' in B1.
data_l5_intro: Data doesn't always fit standard boxes. If a name is too long, it might look cut off. Resizing columns ensures all data is visible. You can manually drag the boundary line between column headers, or double-click it to 'Auto-Fit' the column width to the longest item instantly.
data_l5_action_list: Tap column letter (top) | Drag edge to make wider | Double tap edge to auto-fit
data_l5_task_desc: Type a long sentence in a cell. Make the column wider so it fits.
data_l6_intro: Formatting is about readability, not decoration. Bold headers help distinguish titles from data. Colors can highlight status (Green for Paid, Red for Due). Borders define the table area. Good formatting makes a spreadsheet easy for a human to scan and understand quickly.
data_l6_action_list: Select cells | Tap 'B' for Bold | Tap 'A' icon for Color
data_l6_task_desc: Make the top row of your sheet Bold and Blue.
data_l7_intro: A 'List' or 'Table' is the most common data structure. It must have a 'Header Row' at the top (Row 1) defining categories (e.g., Name, Phone, Email). Consistency is key: do not put a phone number in the email column. Structured data allows for powerful sorting and filtering later.
data_l7_action_list: Col A: Item Name | Col B: Price | Enter 5 items
data_l7_task_desc: Create a grocery list with 5 items and their prices.
data_l8_intro: Sorting organizes chaos. You can reorder a thousand rows instantly. Sorting A-Z (Alphabetical) helps find names. Sorting Smallest-Largest helps find low prices. Sorting by Date puts items in chronological order. Always sort the whole table to keep related data together.
data_l8_action_list: Select Column | Tap 3 dots / More | Sort A-Z
data_l9_intro: Collaboration is Google Sheet's superpower. You can share a live link instead of emailing a static file. You control 'Permissions': 'Viewer' (can only look), 'Commenter' (can suggest), or 'Editor' (can change data). This allows teams to work on the same sheet simultaneously.
data_l9_goal_list: Sharing via link | Viewer vs Editor
data_l9_action_list: Tap Share icon (Person+) | Enter email | OR Copy Link
data_l9_task_desc: Share the link of your sheet with a friend on WhatsApp.
res_l1_intro: Google Search is an index of the web. To find information effectively, you must speak its language: 'Keywords'. Avoid conversational sentences. Instead of asking 'Where can I find a cheap hotel in Delhi for two nights?', distil it to the core concepts: 'Cheap hotel Delhi'. Using fewer, specific words reduces noise and improves result relevance.
res_l1_action_list: Use quotes for exact phrases | Use minus sign to exclude words
res_l2_intro: If the front door is locked, try the window. If your first search fails, iterate with synonyms. Different websites use different terms. If 'Cheap' fails, try 'Budget', 'Affordable', or 'Low cost'. If 'Hotel' fails, try 'Hostel', 'Guesthouse', or 'Stay'. Expanding your vocabulary expands your search results.
res_l2_action_list: Think of 3 words for your topic | Try searching with synonyms
res_l3_intro: The internet is full of misinformation. A Virtual Assistant must be a filter, not just a funnel. Verify the source's credibility. Is it a known news outlet? A government site (.gov)? A university (.edu)? Check the 'About Us' page and the publication date. Old news is often wrong news.
res_l3_action_list: Check the URL | Check the author | Check the date
res_l3_task_desc: Find a news article and check its source.
res_l4_intro: A common task is lead generation: finding contact details. Look beyond the homepage. Check 'Contact Us', 'Team', or 'Press' pages. LinkedIn is the gold standard for professional emails. Sometimes, you must deduce emails based on patterns (e.g., if one employee is jane@company.com, the CEO John is likely john@company.com).
res_l4_action_list: Search 'Company Name + Contact' | Look for 'About Us' page
res_l4_task_desc: Find the email address of a local bakery.
res_l4_quiz_q: Best place to find professional contacts?
res_l5_intro: Clients pay for saved time. Do not send them raw links. Read the information, synthesize the core message, and present it concisely. Use the 'Inverted Pyramid' method: Conclusion first, supporting details second, background info last. A good summary renders the original text unnecessary.
res_l5_action_list: Read the full text | Highlight main ideas | Rewrite in bullet points
res_l5_task_desc: Summarize a Wikipedia paragraph into 3 sentences.
res_l6_intro: Smart researchers don't search every day; they let the search come to them. 'Google Alerts' is a monitoring tool. You set a keyword (e.g., 'Remote Jobs'), and Google emails you whenever a new page matching that term is published. It automates staying up-to-date.
res_l6_action_list: Go to Google Alerts | Enter topic | Set frequency
res_l6_task_desc: Set an alert for your favorite hobby.
res_l7_intro: Businesses succeed by understanding their rivals. Competitor analysis involves listing similar businesses and dissecting them: What are their prices? What do customers say in reviews? What is their social media strategy? This data helps your client identify gaps in the market they can exploit.
res_l7_action_list: Search for similar businesses | Read their reviews | Note their prices
res_l7_task_desc: Find 2 competitors for a pizza shop.
res_l8_intro: Research without organization is clutter. Always capture your findings immediately into a structured Spreadsheet. Use separate columns for 'URL', 'Key Finding', and 'Date Accessed'. This creates a clean database that allows the client to verify your work and access source material easily.
res_l8_action_list: Create a sheet for research | Use columns for Source, Date, Info
res_l8_task_desc: Organize your research links in a spreadsheet.
res_l9_intro: Packaging matters. A professional research report should be clean and readable. Start with an 'Executive Summary' (the answer in 3 lines). Then use bold headings, bullet points, and hyperlinks for the details. A well-formatted document makes the information look valuable and trustworthy.
res_l9_action_list: Start with summary | Use headings | Add sources
res_l9_task_desc: Write a 1-page report on 'Healthy Breakfast Options'.
admin_l1_intro: Email is the standard for formal business communication. It requires structure: A descriptive Subject Line (e.g., 'Invoice for March' not 'Hello'), a polite Salutation, a concise Body, and a professional Sign-off. Avoiding ALL CAPS (shouting) and slang keeps the tone respectful and serious.
admin_l1_action_list: Use clear subjects | Start with 'Dear...' | End with 'Best regards'
admin_l1_task_desc: Draft a professional email to a client.
admin_l2_intro: An admin's job is to protect the client's time. When scheduling, avoid back-and-forth emails. Offer specific slots ('Are you free Tuesday 2PM or Wed 10AM?'). Always be aware of Time Zones. Using Calendar Invites puts the meeting directly on everyone's schedule with reminders.
admin_l2_action_list: Create event | Add guests | Set reminders
admin_l2_task_desc: Schedule a meeting for next Tuesday at 10 AM.
admin_l3_intro: Meetings are useless if decisions are forgotten. 'Minutes' are the official memory of a meeting. You don't transcribe every word. You capture: Who was there, What was decided, and the Action Items (Who does What by When). This document holds people accountable.
admin_l3_action_list: Note attendees | Record key decisions | List next steps
admin_l3_task_desc: Take notes during a mock meeting.
admin_l4_intro: A digital filing system saves hours of searching. Create a logical hierarchy of Folders (e.g., Year > Client > Project). Use consistent naming conventions that include the date (e.g., '2024-05-01_Invoice.pdf'). This allows files to sort chronologically and be found instantly by anyone.
admin_l4_action_list: Create folders by project | Name files consistently (Date_Name)
admin_l4_task_desc: Organize your desktop files into folders.
admin_l5_intro: Travel coordination is about detail. It involves booking logistics (Flights, Hotels, Cabs) within a budget. The final output is an 'Itinerary'—a master document compiling all times, confirmation numbers, and addresses. Checking visa rules and cancellation policies beforehand prevents disasters.
admin_l5_action_list: Compare flights | Book hotels | Create itinerary doc
admin_l5_task_desc: Plan a mock 2-day trip to a nearby city.
admin_l6_intro: Efficiency is the admin's currency. 'Touch Typing' (typing without looking) is a fundamental skill that doubles productivity. Mastering keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+C for Copy, Ctrl+V for Paste, Alt+Tab for Switching Windows) saves seconds that add up to hours over a week.
admin_l6_action_list: Practice touch typing | Use Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V
admin_l6_task_desc: Type a paragraph without looking at the keyboard.
admin_l7_intro: Errors destroy credibility. 'Proofreading' is the final quality check. Read your work backwards or out loud to catch spelling mistakes that your brain usually skips. Don't rely 100% on spell-checkers; they miss context errors (like 'their' vs 'there').
admin_l7_action_list: Read aloud | Use spell check | Check formatting
admin_l7_task_desc: Find 3 errors in a sample text.
admin_l8_intro: Admins hold the keys to the kingdom—passwords, bank details, and strategy. 'Confidentiality' is the ethical duty to keep this secure. Use password managers, never share credentials over chat, and lock your screen when walking away. Your integrity is your most valuable asset.
admin_l8_action_list: Don't share passwords | Lock screen | Shred docs
admin_l9_intro: The modern office is digital. You must be familiar with the 'Tech Stack'. This usually includes a Productivity Suite (Google Workspace/Office 365), Communication tools (Slack/Teams), and Project Management tools (Trello/Asana). Adaptability to new tools is a key job requirement.
admin_l9_action_list: Explore Google Drive | Open Word/Docs | Try Slack/Teams
admin_l9_task_desc: List 3 tools you use for admin work.
supp_l1_intro: Great support is 20% solution and 80% emotion. 'Empathy' is showing you care about the customer's distress. Even if the answer is 'No', delivering it with a kind, understanding tone makes the customer feel valued. Use positive phrasing: 'I can help with that' instead of 'I don't know'.
supp_l1_action_list: Say 'I understand' | Use 'We can' instead of 'I can't'
supp_l1_task_desc: Rewrite 'No, we don't have that' politely.
supp_l2_intro: Most people listen to reply, not to understand. 'Active Listening' involves focusing entirely on the customer. Reflect their problem back to them ('So, if I understand correctly, the device won't turn on?') to confirm alignment. This validates them and ensures you are solving the right problem.
supp_l2_action_list: Repeat back what they said | Ask clarifying questions
supp_l2_task_desc: Practice listening to a friend without interrupting.
supp_l3_intro: Anger is usually fear or frustration. Do not take it personally. The customer is mad at the situation, not you. Stay calm and lower your voice. Let them vent. Apologize for the experience (even if it's not your fault), and pivot to a solution. Your calmness will eventually de-escalate them.
supp_l3_action_list: Don't take it personally | Apologize sincerely | Offer solutions
supp_l4_intro: Efficiency in support comes from 'Templates' or 'Scripts'. For repetitive questions (FAQs), you shouldn't type a new answer every time. Use a pre-written, polished response and customize it with the customer's name. This ensures accuracy, speed, and brand consistency.
supp_l4_action_list: Use templates for FAQs | Personalize the name
supp_l5_intro: Chat is a unique medium: it's real-time like a call but text-based like email. Speed is crucial. Keep sentences short and punchy. Use 'Wait Markers' ('Let me check that for you...') to keep the customer engaged while you research. Always check spelling before hitting send.
supp_l5_action_list: Keep answers short | Check spelling | Use emojis if appropriate
supp_l5_task_desc: Practice typing a quick helpful reply.
supp_l6_intro: Support teams use 'Helpdesks' to manage chaos. Every customer request becomes a 'Ticket' with a unique ID. You must 'Log' interactions, assign a 'Priority' (High/Low), and update the 'Status' (Open/Pending/Resolved). This ensures no customer request falls through the cracks.
supp_l6_action_list: Log every issue | Set priority (High/Low) | Assign to team
supp_l6_task_desc: Create a mock ticket for a 'Broken Item'.
supp_l7_intro: Support is the eyes and ears of the company. Closing the loop involves asking for feedback: 'Did I solve your problem?'. Positive ratings (CSAT) help your career. Negative ratings are learning opportunities. Always thank the customer for their feedback, good or bad.
supp_l7_action_list: Ask for feedback after help | Thank them for reviews
supp_l7_task_desc: Draft a 'How was our service?' email.
supp_l8_intro: Knowing your limits is a skill. If a technical issue is beyond your knowledge, or a customer demands a refund you can't authorize, 'Escalate' the ticket to a senior or specialist. Always provide the senior with a summary of what you've tried so far.
supp_l8_action_list: Identify complex issues | Pass to supervisor with notes
supp_l8_task_desc: Decide if a 'Refund Request' needs a manager.
supp_l9_intro: The end of the interaction is what the customer remembers. Don't just hang up. Ask 'Is there anything else I can help with?' to ensure complete satisfaction. A warm closing ('Have a wonderful week!') leaves a positive emotional residue.
supp_l9_action_list: Ask 'Anything else?' | End on a positive note
supp_l9_task_desc: Write a closing sentence for a chat.
vap_l1_intro: Simulation: Your client is an overwhelmed executive with 500 unread emails. Your goal is 'Inbox Zero'. You must Filter (delete spam), Archive (store old but important info), and Label (categorize into 'Urgent', 'Invoices', 'Clients'). This creates clarity from chaos.
vap_l1_action_list: Sort by date | Delete spam | Create folders
vap_l1_task_desc: Clean up your own email inbox today.
vap_l2_intro: Simulation: Coordinate a high-stakes meeting across continents. Your boss is in London (GMT), the client is in Tokyo (JST). You must use a Time Zone Converter to find a reasonable overlap time. Send a clear Calendar Invite with a Zoom link. One mistake here ruins the deal.
vap_l2_action_list: Find common time | Send invite link
vap_l2_task_desc: Schedule a fake meeting between London and Tokyo.
vap_l3_intro: Simulation: Act as a travel agent. Your client has a conference in Paris with a $1000 budget. You must compare flight durations and hotel locations. Produce a concise 1-page itinerary offering 3 distinct options (Cheapest, Fastest, Best Value).
vap_l3_action_list: Find 3 flight options | Find 3 hotels within budget
vap_l3_task_desc: Create a 1-page travel plan for a boss.
vap_l4_intro: Simulation: Digitization task. You receive a scanned PDF of handwritten contacts. You must type them into Google Sheets. Attention to detail is paramount—one wrong digit makes a phone number useless. You will format columns correctly (Text vs Number) to ensure usability.
vap_l4_action_list: Enter data from PDF to Sheet | Format headers
vap_l4_task_desc: Create a contact list spreadsheet with 5 rows.
vap_l5_intro: Simulation: Crisis management. A loyal customer emails, furious about a delayed refund. Draft a response that acknowledges their anger, explains the situation transparently, and provides a concrete timeline for the solution. Turn a detractor into a promoter through empathy.
vap_l5_task_desc: Reply to a customer asking for a refund.
vap_l6_intro: Simulation: Visual communication. Create a 'About Me' slide for a client pitch deck. Use the rule of thirds: clear Title, bulleted content (not paragraphs), and a high-quality image. Design it to be read in 5 seconds or less.
vap_l6_action_list: Add title | Add bullet points | Add image
vap_l7_intro: Simulation: Audio processing. You are given a 2-minute voice memo from a meeting. Type it out word-for-word. Indicate speakers (Speaker A, Speaker B) and timestamps. This document becomes the official record of truth for the team.
vap_l7_action_list: Listen to audio | Type exactly what is said
vap_l7_task_desc: Transcribe 1 minute of a YouTube video.
vap_l8_intro: Simulation: Content planning. A coffee shop needs a week of Instagram content. Create a calendar: Mon (Motivation), Wed (Product Video), Fri (Weekend Offer). Write the captions and select placeholder images. Planning ahead ensures consistency.
vap_l8_action_list: Pick date | Write caption | Select image
vap_l8_task_desc: Plan 3 social media posts for a week.
vap_l9_intro: Simulation: Getting paid. You have completed the work. Now create a professional invoice PDF. It must list your contact details, the client's details, an itemized list of services ('Admin Support - 5 Hours'), the rate, and the total due. This is a legal demand for payment.
vap_l9_action_list: Add your info | Add client info | List services and cost
aib_l1_intro: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not future magic; it is present-day math. It is software that mimics human cognition. When your phone unlocks by recognizing your face, that is Computer Vision. When Maps routes you around traffic, that is Predictive AI. When Netflix suggests a movie, that is a Recommendation Engine. You are likely already an AI user without knowing it.
aib_l1_goal_list: Recognizing AI features | AI in daily life
aib_l1_action_list: Face unlock? That is AI. | Voice search? That is AI. | YouTube suggestions? That is AI.
aib_l1_task_desc: Find one feature on your phone that uses AI (like Face Unlock or Smart Reply).
aib_l2_intro: Traditional computers follow explicit rules ('If A, do B'). AI uses 'Machine Learning' to find patterns in data. You show it a million photos of cats, and it learns what a cat 'looks' like. It can then recognize a cat in a new photo it has never seen before. It is a prediction machine, not just a calculator.
aib_l2_goal_list: It is software | It learns patterns
aib_l2_action_list: It is computer code | It learns from examples | It can see, hear, and write
aib_l2_task_desc: Explain to a friend: 'AI is a computer that learns like a student.'
aib_l3_intro: AI is the silent engine of the internet. 'Spam Filters' in Gmail use AI to read and block junk mail. 'Autocorrect' predicts your next word based on your typing habits. 'Camera Filters' on Instagram use AI to map your face in 3D and apply effects. These tools augment your abilities, making you faster and more efficient.
aib_l3_action_list: Google Maps traffic | Spelling autocorrect | Camera filters
aib_l3_task_desc: Type a wrong word in WhatsApp and see if AI corrects it.
aib_l4_intro: Generative AI (like ChatGPT or Gemini) is a new type of AI that creates new content. You interact with it via 'Prompting'. The quality of the answer depends on the quality of your question. A vague prompt gets a vague answer. A detailed, specific prompt gets a high-quality, tailored result. This is the skill of the future.
aib_l4_action_list: Ask: 'Recipe for tea' | Ask: 'Write a sick leave msg' | Ask: 'Joke about cats'
aib_l4_task_desc: Use an AI chat (like this app) to ask: 'How to boil an egg?'
aib_l5_intro: Computer Vision allows phones to 'see'. Google Lens is a visual search engine. You can point your camera at a flower to identify its species, at a math problem to see the solution, or at a menu in a foreign language to translate it instantly. It bridges the gap between the physical world and digital information.
aib_l5_action_list: Open Google Lens | Point at flower -> Identifies it | Point at English text -> Translates it
aib_l5_task_desc: Use Google Lens to translate a product label in your kitchen.
aib_l6_intro: Speech Recognition converts audio waves into text. Voice Typing (Dictation) is often 3x faster than thumb typing. It allows you to draft emails, notes, or messages while your hands are busy. Modern AI understands accents and context, making it highly accurate for daily use.
aib_l6_action_list: Tap Mic on keyboard | Speak clearly | Watch it type
aib_l6_task_desc: Send a WhatsApp message to a friend using only your voice.
aib_l7_intro: Neural Machine Translation has broken language barriers. Apps like Google Translate don't just swap words; they understand sentences. You can have a bilingual conversation where the phone listens to Hindi and speaks English, acting as a real-time interpreter. This opens up global knowledge to everyone.
aib_l7_action_list: Use Google Translate | Type in Hindi -> Output English | Listen to pronunciation
aib_l7_task_desc: Translate 'Hello, how are you?' into 3 different languages.
aib_l8_intro: AI is a statistical model, not a fact database. It predicts the next likely word. Sometimes, it confidently predicts wrong information; this is called a 'Hallucination'. Never use AI for medical advice or critical facts without verifying on Google. Use it for creativity and drafting, but trust your own judgment for facts.
aib_l8_action_list: AI can lie (Hallucinate) | Always check facts | Don't share secrets
aib_l8_task_desc: Ask AI a question you know the answer to (e.g. 'Who is my mother?'). See if it knows (it shouldn't!).
aib_l9_intro: AI is not a replacement for humans; it is a bicycle for the mind. It amplifies your effort. A writer using AI can write faster. A coder using AI can code faster. The future belongs to those who partner with AI to do the boring work, leaving the creative and strategic work for themselves.
aib_l9_action_list: You are the pilot | AI is the engine | Use it to work faster
aib_l9_task_desc: Think of one task you do daily (e.g., writing list) that AI could help with.
chat_l1_intro: Chatting with AI is a skill called 'Prompt Engineering'. Think of the AI as a very smart but literal intern. If you say 'Write an email', it will write a generic one. If you say 'Write a polite email to a angry client apologizing for a delay', it will write a perfect one. The secret is: Context + Task + Tone.
chat_l1_action_list: Be specific | Give examples | Ask for format
chat_l1_task_desc: Ask AI to explain gravity to a 5-year-old.
chat_l2_intro: You can assign a 'Persona' to the AI. Telling it 'Act as a Senior Marketing Manager' or 'Act as a Primary School Teacher' drastically changes its output. The AI accesses different parts of its training data to match the vocabulary and expertise of the role you assign.
chat_l2_action_list: Tell AI: 'You are a teacher' | Explain the situation
chat_l2_task_desc: Tell AI to act as a travel agent and plan a trip.
chat_l3_intro: The first answer is rarely the best. AI works best in conversation. If the output is too long, say 'Make it shorter'. If it's too complex, say 'Explain like I am 10'. This back-and-forth process is called 'Iteration'. Don't accept the first draft; sculpt it.
chat_l3_task_desc: Ask AI for a recipe, then ask to make it vegan.
chat_l4_intro: AI is an infinite simulator. You can use it to practice difficult conversations. Ask it to 'Act as an interviewer for a graphic design job'. It will ask you questions, wait for your reply, and then give you feedback. This allows you to fail safely and learn quickly.
chat_l4_task_desc: Roleplay a job interview with AI.
chat_l5_intro: In the information age, we drown in data. AI is a compression tool. You can paste a 10-page report or a messy transcript into the chat and ask 'Summarize the top 3 action items'. It extracts the signal from the noise instantly, saving you hours of reading.
chat_l5_action_list: Paste long text | Ask 'Summarize in bullet points'
chat_l5_task_desc: Paste a news article and ask for a summary.
chat_l6_intro: Writer's block is a thing of the past. AI is an idea machine. It can generate 50 names for a bakery or 20 blog post ideas in seconds. Most will be average, but one might be brilliant. Use AI to get the volume of ideas, then use your human judgment to pick the quality.
chat_l6_task_desc: Ask for 5 gift ideas for a friend.
chat_l7_intro: You can dictate the shape of the answer. Text blocks are hard to read. Ask AI to 'Output as a Table', 'Create a Checklist', or 'Write a CSV'. Structured data is easier to copy-paste into Excel or Slides, fitting seamlessly into your workflow.
chat_l7_action_list: Ask 'Output as a table' | 'Output as a CSV'
chat_l7_task_desc: Ask for a comparison table of apples and oranges.
chat_l8_intro: Trust but verify. AI 'hallucinates' because it predicts words, it doesn't query a database of truth. If AI gives you a specific fact (like a population number or a historical date), always double-check it with a Google Search. AI is for logic and creativity; Google is for facts.
chat_l8_action_list: Don't trust blindly | Verify important facts
chat_l8_task_desc: Ask AI a fact, then verify it on Google.
chat_l9_intro: AI has boundaries. It has a 'Knowledge Cutoff' (it may not know yesterday's news). It cannot feel emotions, make moral judgments, or take physical actions. Understanding what AI *cannot* do prevents frustration and helps you use it for what it *can* do best.
chat_l9_action_list: Know cut-off dates | Avoid harmful prompts
chat_l9_task_desc: Ask AI about something that happened today (it might not know).
tool_l1_intro: Writing is being revolutionized. Google Docs now features 'Help me write'. You can type a rough bullet list of ideas, and the AI will expand it into a polished formal letter. It conquers the 'Blank Page Syndrome', giving you a first draft to edit rather than starting from zero.
tool_l1_task_desc: Use AI in Google Docs to write a cover letter.
tool_l2_intro: Spreadsheet formulas are complex languages. AI acts as a translator. In Google Sheets, you can simply ask 'Write a formula to sum column A if column B says Paid'. The AI writes the code for you. You focus on the data logic; AI handles the syntax.
tool_l2_task_desc: Use AI to create a budget template in Sheets.
tool_l3_intro: Creating presentations is often tedious formatting work. AI tools can now generate entire slide decks from a single topic prompt. 'Create a 5-slide pitch for a bakery' generates titles, bullet points, and even selects relevant stock images. Your job shifts from 'creator' to 'editor'.
tool_l3_task_desc: Generate a presentation outline on 'Climate Change'.
tool_l4_intro: Email is the biggest time sink in business. Gmail's AI ('Help me write') can draft replies based on the context of the thread. It can formalize a messy note or shorten a long rant. It helps you maintain professional communication standards even when you are in a rush.
tool_l4_task_desc: Use AI to write a polite decline email.
tool_l5_intro: Coding is no longer just for engineers. AI acts as a 'Co-pilot'. You can describe a simple tool ('Make a website button that turns green when clicked') in plain English, and AI will write the HTML/CSS code. This democratizes the ability to build simple digital tools.
tool_l5_action_list: Ask for simple code | Explain code
tool_l5_task_desc: Ask AI to write a simple HTML button code.
tool_l6_intro: Notion combines notes and AI. It acts as a smart editor. You can highlight a messy paragraph of meeting notes and click 'Ask AI > Improve writing' or 'Make shorter'. It cleans up your thoughts, summarizes pages, and generates action items instantly.
tool_l6_action_list: Use AI block | Ask to improve writing
tool_l6_task_desc: Use Notion AI to summarize a page.
tool_l7_intro: Canva's 'Magic Studio' brings AI to design. 'Magic Edit' allows you to select an object (like a red shirt) and type 'change to blue suit' to swap it realistically. 'Text to Image' generates custom stock photos from descriptions. Professional design effects are now accessible via simple text commands.
tool_l7_task_desc: Generate an image of a 'Cyberpunk Cat' in Canva.
tool_l8_intro: You should listen in meetings, not scribble notes. AI tools like Otter.ai or Fireflies.ai join your calls, record audio, transcribe it to text, and—most importantly—summarize the key decisions. This creates a perfect searchable record of every conversation without human effort.
tool_l8_task_desc: Use an AI tool to summarize a recorded voice note.
tool_l9_intro: The ultimate productivity hack is letting apps talk to each other. Tools like Zapier use 'If This Then That' logic. AI now helps you build these automations. You say 'Save Gmail attachments to Dropbox', and AI configures the connection. This automates repetitive admin work entirely.
tool_l9_task_desc: Understand a simple automation: 'If email received -> save attachment'.
voi_l1_intro: Voice Typing (Dictation) transforms speech to text instantly. Found on Gboard and iOS keyboards (Mic icon), it uses AI to recognize words. It handles punctuation ('comma', 'full stop') and allows you to draft long messages while walking or cooking, maximizing productivity during 'dead time'.
voi_l1_task_desc: Write a note using only your voice.
voi_l2_intro: The 'Conversation Mode' in Google Translate is a portable interpreter. It listens to two languages simultaneously. You speak English, it speaks Hindi; they speak Hindi, it speaks English. This real-time mediation removes language barriers in travel or business negotiations.
voi_l2_task_desc: Have a conversation with someone in another language using the app.
voi_l3_intro: Live Caption creates subtitles for the real world. Available on Android/Chrome, it generates text for ANY audio playing on your device—videos, podcasts, or voice notes—even with the sound off. It is crucial for accessibility (deaf/hard of hearing) and useful for consuming content in quiet places.
voi_l3_action_list: Turn on Live Captions on Android/Chrome
voi_l3_task_desc: Watch a video on mute with captions.
voi_l4_intro: Google Search includes a pronunciation coach. Searching 'How to pronounce [Word]' brings up a tool where you can listen to the word and then speak it into your mic. AI analyzes your audio waveform and gives specific feedback on which sounds you mispronounced.
voi_l4_action_list: Ask 'How to pronounce X' | Listen and repeat
voi_l5_intro: Voice Assistants (Google/Siri) understand 'Chained Commands'. You can say complex instructions like 'Set a timer for 10 minutes AND play jazz music'. NLP (Natural Language Processing) parses this sentence, separates the two commands, and executes both. This is the peak of hands-free control.
voi_l5_task_desc: Set a timer for 5 minutes using voice.
voi_l6_intro: The Pixel Recorder app (and similar tools) perform 'Diarization'—identifying different speakers in a recording. It provides a searchable transcript. You can search for the word 'Budget' in an hour-long audio file, and the app will jump to the exact second that word was spoken.
voi_l6_task_desc: Record yourself speaking and read the transcript.
voi_l7_intro: Screen readers like 'TalkBack' (Android) or 'VoiceOver' (iOS) allow blind users to navigate phones via touch and sound. They read aloud every button you touch. Understanding these tools helps us design inclusive content (like adding Alt Text to images) so everyone can access the digital world.
voi_l7_action_list: Understand how blind people use phones
voi_l8_intro: Language learning apps like Duolingo now feature AI Roleplay. You can text or speak with an AI character in a safe environment. The AI adjusts its vocabulary level to match yours and corrects grammar mistakes gently, removing the fear of embarrassment often felt in human practice.
voi_l8_action_list: Talk to AI in target language
voi_l9_intro: When traveling, your phone is a universal translator. Pointing your camera at a menu translates the food. Asking Maps for directions in the local language helps taxi drivers understand. These multimodal AI tools (Vision + Voice + Map) are essential for modern navigation.
voi_l9_action_list: Use Lens to translate menus | Use voice to ask directions
voi_l9_task_desc: Pretend to order food in French using app.
aip_l1_intro: Great projects start with clear definitions. Before building, you must define the 'Problem Statement'. Instead of 'I want a website', say 'I need a platform to connect stray dogs with adopters in Mumbai'. A specific problem allows AI to give specific solutions.
aip_l1_action_list: Identify a real problem | Define success
aip_l1_task_desc: Define a problem you want to solve (e.g. Meal Planning).
aip_l2_intro: AI excels at breaking big tasks into small steps. Ask it: 'Create a step-by-step roadmap to launch a dog adoption site'. It will list phases: 1. Content Gathering, 2. Site Design, 3. Launch. This turns an overwhelming goal into a manageable checklist.
aip_l2_action_list: Ask AI for a plan | Break down tasks
aip_l2_task_desc: Ask AI for a 5-step plan to solve your problem.
aip_l3_intro: The 'Zero to One' problem is the hardest part of creating. Use AI to generate the 'Draft'. Ask it to write the About Us page, suggest a logo concept, or list dog breed descriptions. The goal is not perfection, but to have something on the page to edit.
aip_l3_action_list: Use AI to generate first draft
aip_l3_task_desc: Generate the core content for your project.
aip_l4_intro: AI is the generator; you are the curator. Review the AI draft. Is the tone right? Is the information accurate for your city? Add your 'Human Touch'—local slang, specific details, and emotional nuance. This 'Human-in-the-Loop' process creates quality work.
aip_l4_action_list: Ask AI to improve specific parts | Correct errors
aip_l4_task_desc: Refine one section of your project.
aip_l5_intro: Visuals build trust. Use AI image generators to create assets if you lack photos. Ask AI for a 'Color Palette' that conveys trust and warmth (e.g., Blues and Yellows). Consistent visuals make your project look professional and cohesive.
aip_l5_task_desc: Create/Select one visual for your project.
aip_l6_intro: Your work needs a container. Organize your text and images into a clear format, like a Slide Deck or a PDF One-pager. Use headings to guide the reader. AI can structure this for you: 'Outline a 5-slide pitch deck for this project'.
aip_l6_task_desc: Arrange your content into a simple doc or slide.
aip_l7_intro: You can simulate user testing with AI. Paste your project text and ask: 'Act as a critic. What is missing from this plan?'. The AI will find gaps you missed (e.g., 'You forgot a contact form'). This virtual feedback loop strengthens your work before you show it to real people.
aip_l7_action_list: Ask AI to critique your work | Ask a friend
aip_l8_intro: The last 10% of work makes 90% of the difference. Check for spelling errors, broken links, and formatting alignment. A polished project signals competence. Use tools like Grammarly or spell-check to ensure it is error-free.
aip_l8_task_desc: Do a final review of your project.
aip_l9_intro: True learning happens during reflection. Ask yourself: What was easy? What was hard? How did AI help? How did it fail? Documenting these 'Lessons Learned' ensures you improve your process for the next project.
aip_l9_action_list: Note what went well | What to do better next time
aip_l9_task_desc: Write 1 sentence about what you learned.
loc_l1_intro: The 'Digital Mindset' is the realization that the customer journey begins online. Before walking into a shop, a customer searches for it on their phone. If a business is invisible on Google Maps or Instagram, it effectively does not exist for modern consumers. Your job is to build this digital bridge.
loc_l2_intro: The Digital Customer Journey has 4 stages: 1. Discovery (Search), 2. Evaluation (Reviews/Photos), 3. Action (Call/Visit), 4. Retention (Loyalty). A digital helper optimizes each stage. You ensure they are found, look trustworthy, are easy to contact, and stay connected via social media.
loc_l2_action_list: Map steps: Search -> Find -> Call -> Buy
loc_l2_task_desc: Draw the path of a customer buying a cake.
loc_l3_intro: In the absence of physical interaction, customers rely on 'Trust Signals'. These are digital indicators of quality: A 4.5+ Star Rating, recent positive reviews, high-quality photos, and an active social media presence. Helping a business improve these signals directly increases their customer footfall.
loc_l3_task_desc: Identify 2 trust signals on a website.
loc_l4_intro: Frictionless payment is key to sales. A Merchant QR Code (Paytm/PhonePe Business) allows a shop to accept UPI payments easily. Unlike personal codes, Merchant codes provide daily settlement reports and voice notifications ('Paytm received...'), which helps shopkeepers track revenue separately from personal funds.
loc_l4_action_list: Set up merchant QR | Learn to share payment links
loc_l5_intro: For food businesses, aggregators like Zomato/Swiggy are vital marketing channels. They charge a commission but provide a massive customer base and delivery fleet. Your role is to help the shopkeeper with the paperwork (FSSAI license, Menu digitization) to get listed on these platforms.
loc_l6_intro: Social media is the new word-of-mouth. A business needs a Facebook Page and an Instagram Professional Account. Consistency beats virality. Posting simple updates—'Fresh Stock Arrived', 'Festival Sale Today'—keeps the business top-of-mind for local customers.
loc_l6_task_desc: Create a bio for a business Instagram.
loc_l7_intro: Reviews are a public conversation. Never ignore them. Replying to positive reviews builds loyalty. Replying to negative reviews shows you care. A polite response to a complaint ('Sorry for the delay, we are fixing it') can turn a bad situation into a display of good customer service for everyone else reading.
loc_l7_action_list: Reply to all reviews | Ask happy clients for review
loc_l7_task_desc: Write a reply to a 5-star review.
loc_l8_intro: Local SEO helps a shop appear in 'Near Me' searches. The golden rule is NAP Consistency: Name, Address, and Phone Number must be identical across Google, Facebook, and Justdial. Using local keywords in the description (e.g., 'Best Saree Shop in Dadar West') helps Google match the shop to local searchers.
loc_l8_action_list: Use city name in description | Accurate category
loc_l8_task_desc: Write a business description with local keywords.
loc_l9_intro: To get hired by a shopkeeper, focus on Value, not Tech. Don't say 'I can do SEO'. Say 'I can help more customers find your shop on Google Maps'. Show them a competitor who is doing well online to create a desire for your service.
loc_l9_task_desc: Practice a 1-minute pitch to a shop owner.
gbpa_l1_intro: A 'Verified' Google Business Profile isn't enough; it must be 'Optimized'. This means filling every single field. Add the 'Opening Date', add specific 'Attributes' (like WiFi availability), and write a 750-character description packed with keywords. Complete profiles rank higher in search results.
gbpa_l1_action_list: Fill every field | Use keywords in description
gbpa_l1_task_desc: Check a profile for missing info.
gbpa_l2_intro: Google loves fresh content. Don't just upload photos once. A profile that uploads new photos weekly gets 42% more requests for directions. Strategy: Upload 1 Exterior shot (easy to find), 1 Interior shot (ambiance), and 1 Product/Team shot every week to show the business is active.
gbpa_l2_action_list: Upload weekly photos | Use good lighting
gbpa_l2_task_desc: Plan 3 photos to upload this week.
gbpa_l3_intro: The Q&A section is often empty. You don't have to wait for customers. You can post your own FAQs! Post questions like 'Do you have parking?' or 'Is this veg-only?' and answer them immediately as the 'Owner'. This pre-empts customer doubts and improves conversion.
gbpa_l3_action_list: Post your own FAQs | Answer them clearly
gbpa_l4_intro: Google Posts act like mini social media updates directly on Maps. Use 'Update' for news, 'Offer' for coupons (with start/end dates), and 'Event' for sales. These posts appear when people search for you, giving them an immediate reason to visit right now.
gbpa_l4_action_list: Create an 'Update' post | Add a button
gbpa_l4_task_desc: Draft an update post about a sale.
gbpa_l5_intro: Advanced SEO Tip: Use keywords in your review replies. If a customer writes 'Great food', reply with 'Thanks for loving our [Butter Chicken], it is our specialty!'. This reinforces to Google that your restaurant is relevant for the keyword 'Butter Chicken'. Be natural, do not spam.
gbpa_l5_action_list: Include service name in reply | Thank customer
gbpa_l5_task_desc: Write a keyword-rich reply to a review.
gbpa_l6_intro: The 'Performance' tab is your report card. 'Queries' shows what words people typed to find you. 'Platform' shows if they came from Maps or Search. 'Actions' shows if they called or visited the website. Use this data to tell the shop owner: '50 people called you from Google last month'.
gbpa_l6_action_list: Check how people found you | Check button clicks
gbpa_l6_task_desc: Look at insights (mock data) and find top search term.
gbpa_l7_intro: Maps can be messy. Competitors may create fake listings or leave fake 1-star reviews. You can help by clicking 'Suggest an Edit' to remove fake duplicates or 'Report' to flag violation reviews. Keeping the map clean helps legitimate businesses shine.
gbpa_l7_action_list: Report fake reviews | Fix wrong info
gbpa_l7_task_desc: Learn how to 'Suggest an Edit' on Maps.
gbpa_l8_intro: For businesses without a shop (like plumbers or electricians), do not pin your home address. Instead, set 'Service Areas'—a list of pincodes or city names where you work. This tells Google to show your profile to customers in those zones without revealing your private home location.
gbpa_l8_action_list: Set accurate service areas | Don't over-expand
gbpa_l9_intro: Google offers a free, auto-generated website for every profile. It pulls your photos, posts, and reviews into a simple one-page site. While basic, it is perfect for small shops that have no budget. It updates automatically whenever you update your Google Profile.
gbpa_l9_action_list: Use 'Website' tab | Publish free Google site
wam_l1_intro: A 'Broadcast List' is the professional way to mass message. Unlike a Group, where everyone sees each other's numbers (privacy risk), a Broadcast sends individual messages. It feels personal. Crucial Rule: The receiver MUST have your number saved, or they will not receive the message (this prevents spam).
wam_l1_action_list: Create broadcast list | Add contacts (they must save your number)
wam_l2_intro: WhatsApp Status is high-engagement real estate. People view it voluntarily. Post 3-5 times a day to stay visible. Use the 'Mix' strategy: 1 Product photo, 1 Customer Review, 1 Behind-the-scenes video. Since statuses disappear in 24 hours, they create 'FOMO' (Fear Of Missing Out), driving quicker sales.
wam_l2_action_list: Post product photos | Share reviews | Post offers
wam_l2_task_desc: Create a status update for a sale.
wam_l3_intro: A messy catalog loses sales. Use 'Collections' to organize items (e.g., 'Menswear', 'Womenswear', 'Sale'). This acts like folders. Instead of sharing the whole shop link, you can send a specific Collection Link to a customer asking for 'Men's Shirts', making their shopping experience easier.
wam_l3_action_list: Group items into collections | Share collection links
wam_l4_intro: Know the difference. 'Groups' are for discussion (everyone talks); good for small teams. 'Communities' are for announcements (only admins talk); good for large customer bases. Use Communities to send updates to 2000+ people without the chaos of everyone replying 'Good Morning'.
wam_l4_action_list: Use groups for chat | Use Communities for announcements
wam_l4_task_desc: Decide if you need a group or community for a school.
wam_l5_intro: Labels turn WhatsApp into a CRM (Customer Relationship Manager). Use them as a pipeline. Label 1: 'New Inquiry'. Label 2: 'Order Placed'. Label 3: 'Payment Pending'. Label 4: 'Completed'. Move a chat from one label to the next as the deal progresses. This ensures you never forget to collect payment.
wam_l6_intro: Advanced automation: Schedule your 'Away Message'. Set it to trigger ONLY outside business hours (e.g., 8 PM to 9 AM). This sets professional boundaries, protecting your personal time while politely informing customers that you will reply in the morning.
wam_l6_action_list: Refine away message | Schedule specific times
wam_l6_task_desc: Set away message for lunch break.
wam_l7_intro: Reduce friction with 'wa.me' links. Format: `wa.me/919999999999`. You can add a pre-filled message code (`?text=I want to buy`). When a user clicks this link on Instagram or a Website, it opens WhatsApp with the message already typed. They just have to hit send.
wam_l7_action_list: Create wa.me link | Add pre-filled message
wam_l7_task_desc: Create a link that says 'I want to order'.
wam_l8_intro: Protect your brand and sanity. Configure privacy so only 'Contacts' can see your Status or add you to Groups. This prevents competitors from spying on your offers and stops spammers from adding you to random groups.
wam_l8_action_list: Control who sees DP | Control who adds to groups
wam_l8_quiz_q: You can stop people adding you to groups?
wam_l9_intro: A 'Campaign' is a coordinated push. Don't just do one thing. 1. Change Profile Photo to Sale Poster. 2. Post 5 Status updates. 3. Send a Broadcast to warm leads. 4. Use Labels to track interest. Executing all these steps together creates a 'buzz' that drives sales.
wam_l9_task_desc: Write a plan: 1 Status, 1 Broadcast, 1 Catalog update.
web_l1_intro: A 'Landing Page' is different from a 'Website'. A website has many distractions (About, Blog, Team). A Landing Page has ONE goal: Conversion. It has one button (Call to Action) and removes all other navigation. Use this when running an ad or a specific offer.
web_l1_task_desc: Draw a landing page on paper.
web_l2_intro: Carrd.co is the best tool for one-page sites. It is a 'No-Code' builder. You start with a 'Template' (pre-made design) and modify 'Elements' (Text, Image, Buttons). It treats web design like building blocks, making it accessible to non-technical users.
web_l3_intro: Canva now publishes websites. If you can design a poster, you can design a site. It's visual-first. While not good for complex stores, it is perfect for visual portfolios, event invitations, or restaurant menus. You hit 'Publish' and get a free link instantly.
web_l3_task_desc: Design a portfolio site in Canva.
web_l4_intro: Design attracts, but Copy sells. 'Copywriting' is persuasive writing. Your 'Headline' must hook the reader in 3 seconds by stating the benefit. Focus on 'You' (the customer), not 'We' (the business). Example: 'Get Fit Fast' is better than 'We offer gym services'.
web_l4_action_list: Write a catchy headline | List 3 benefits
web_l5_intro: The 'Call to Action' (CTA) is the most important button. It tells the user what to do next. Use action verbs and urgency. Instead of 'Submit', use 'Get My Free Guide'. Instead of 'Contact', use 'Book a Call Now'. Make the button color stand out from the background.
web_l5_action_list: Use strong verbs (Buy, Join, Call) | Make button big
web_l6_intro: The web is connected by 'Hyperlinks'. You can link a button to a URL, a WhatsApp chat, a phone dialer (`tel:999`), or an email (`mailto:abc@com`). Test every link before publishing. A broken link is a broken trust signal.
web_l6_action_list: Link button to WhatsApp | Link icons to Instagram
web_l6_task_desc: Add a WhatsApp link to your button.
web_l7_intro: 70% of web traffic is mobile. Designing for desktop first is a mistake. Always check the 'Mobile View' editor. Ensure font sizes are readable (16px+) and buttons are thumb-friendly (large enough to tap without zooming). This is called 'Responsive Design'.
web_l7_action_list: Switch to mobile view | Check font size
web_l7_task_desc: Check your site on a phone screen.
web_l8_intro: Going live involves a URL. Free tools give you a 'Sub-domain' (e.g., `myshop.carrd.co`). This is fine for starting. Keep the URL short, simple, and easy to spell so you can share it verbally or via text. Once you grow, you can buy a custom domain (`myshop.com`).
web_l8_task_desc: Publish your site and share the link.
web_l9_intro: Publishing is not the end; it is the start. 'Analytics' tracks visitor behavior. 'Views' are how many people saw the page. 'Clicks' are how many took action. The 'Conversion Rate' (Clicks divided by Views) tells you how effective your design is. Use this data to improve.
web_l9_action_list: Check how many viewed the site (if available)
web_l9_task_desc: Look for view count on dashboard.
cli_l1_intro: First impressions matter. 'Onboarding' is the structured process of welcoming a new client. Send a 'Welcome Packet' email that includes: A thank you note, a list of what you need from them (passwords, logos), and a timeline. This establishes you as a professional, not just a helper.
cli_l1_action_list: Send welcome email | Ask for requirements
cli_l1_task_desc: Draft a welcome message for a new client.
cli_l2_intro: Stop quoting prices in chat. Send a 'Proposal'. This is a document outlining: The Problem, Your Solution, The Timeline, and The Investment (Price). A proposal frames your price as an investment in a solution, making it easier for the client to say 'Yes'.
cli_l2_action_list: Outline what you will do | State price clearly
cli_l2_task_desc: Write a simple proposal for logo design.
cli_l3_intro: A contract is not about mistrust; it is about clarity. It prevents 'Scope Creep' (when clients add extra work for free). Even a simple email agreement stating 'I will do X, Y, Z for ₹5000 by Friday' acts as a contract. Always get this agreement in writing before starting.
cli_l3_task_desc: Read a simple freelance contract template.
cli_l4_intro: An invoice is a professional demand for payment. It must include: The word 'Invoice', a unique Invoice Number, Date, Your Details, Client Details, Line items of work, Total, and Payment Methods (UPI/Bank). Sending accurate invoices promptly ensures you get paid faster.
cli_l4_action_list: Send invoice promptly | Include payment link
cli_l5_intro: The biggest client fear is being ghosted. Proactive communication kills anxiety. Send a 'Weekly Update' every Friday, even if the update is just 'Everything is on track'. Silence is interpreted as trouble. Keep the client informed to keep them happy.
cli_l5_action_list: Weekly updates | Use email for formal info
cli_l6_intro: You teach clients how to treat you. If you answer calls at 10 PM on Sunday, they will expect it forever. Set clear 'Business Hours'. State them in your email signature. Politely decline work outside these hours. Respected boundaries lead to a sustainable career.
cli_l6_action_list: State work hours | Say no to extra unpaid work
cli_l6_task_desc: Politely decline a call on Sunday.
cli_l7_intro: Feedback is the breakfast of champions. Don't guess if the client is happy; ask. 'Is there anything I could have done better?'. Receiving criticism without getting defensive is a hallmark of professionalism. Use it to improve your next project.
cli_l7_action_list: Ask 'How can I improve?' | Don't take criticism personally
cli_l7_task_desc: Ask for feedback on a finished project.
cli_l8_intro: It is 5x easier to sell to an existing client than a new one. 'Upselling' is offering more value. If you designed a logo, ask 'Do you also need business cards?'. If you wrote a blog, ask 'Do you need social media posts for this?'. Increase your income by solving more problems.
cli_l9_intro: A referral is the highest compliment. When a client is happy, ask: 'Do you know anyone else who needs this service?'. People trust recommendations from friends. Building a referral engine means you spend less time hunting for work and more time doing it.
cli_l9_action_list: Ask happy clients to refer friends
